Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear note and the invoice.

Short answers up front: we can investigate and, depending on evidence, either issue a credit note that removes the VAT or provide a refund. There are two things we need to confirm before Finance can process:

- VAT ID provenance: we need a timestamped confirmation that the IE VAT ID was valid on or before the invoice date (2025-05-15). A VIES lookup screenshot or an official VAT registration letter showing active status on or before 2025-05-15 will suffice.
- Nature of supply: confirm whether NimbusCloud was charged as a marketplace seller or end-customer for the line items in INV-453. For marketplace-routing there are different rules and possibly self-billing implications.

Ben — can you kick off a recredit ticket with Finance and block out the VAT portion until Vivek/Tax have reviewed? If we can't validate an earlier VAT registration, we usually can't apply the reverse-charge retroactively.

Oliver — if you can share the VIES screenshot / VAT cert by end of week we'll aim to respond within 3 business days of receipt.

Regards,

Hi all — thanks for the details and the patience while we checked tax records.

We validated the supplied VAT ID (IE1234567) against VIES. The first successful validation in VIES is dated 2025-05-28, which is after the invoice date (2025-05-15). Based on Irish VAT rules and Redwood's VAT policy: we cannot treat the original sale as reverse-charged retroactively without evidence the VAT ID was active on or before the invoice date.

Options for NimbusCloud:
1) If Nimbus can provide authoritative evidence that the VAT ID was active before 2025-05-15 (e.g., dated certificate, historic VIES record with timestamp, or tax authority letter), we'll reprocess and issue a credit note that removes the VAT amount and reissue a net invoice. This will be clearly documented in our journals and reflected in the May tax submission as an adjustment.

2) If no earlier evidence exists, Redwood can issue a customer credit for the VAT portion as a goodwill accommodation. This will not change the original VAT reporting (we would have reported VAT in May), and accounting will treat the credit as a post-period contra-revenue/credit — please note this may have differing tax consequences for Nimbus depending on your local reclaim process.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Oliver: send the best evidence you have (VIES screenshot with timestamp or VAT certificate). If evidence arrives and validates, we will target 7 business days to issue the credit note and reissued invoice.
- If no evidence, confirm whether Nimbus prefers a cash refund or a customer credit applied to the next invoice; Redwood can process a credit within 5 business days of confirmation.

I've attached a pro forma credit-note stub showing the VAT to be reversed for visibility.

Attachment: redwood_credit_note_453.csv (csv)

Tax reference docs: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcDEF234tax-evidence
